title: Surjectivity of a coherent formal-system map is detected modulo the ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal. A morphism $(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ in the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], which is abelian [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] in the sense of [def-sp-abelian], is an epimorphism if and only if its component $\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal G_1$ is an epimorphism in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Y (lemma-inverse-systems-surjective, line 6396); proof 'Omitted. Hint: Look on affine opens, use Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) and Algebra, Lemma 00DV (algebra-lemma-NAK, Nakayama's lemma)'. 'Surjective' in an abelian category means Coker = 0 (Homology, Definition 010B), equivalently epimorphism (Lemma 010C (2)).

proof.text: (Reduction to the cokernels.) Let $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ be a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and let $q_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n$ be the cokernel of $\alpha_n$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], as in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (the $\mathcal F_n,\mathcal G_n$ are coherent, hence quasi-coherent). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian, hence preadditive, and $q=(q_n):(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal C_n)$ is a cokernel of $\alpha$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero] (Stacks 010C (2)) applied in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\alpha$ is an epimorphism iff $(\mathcal C_n)$ is a zero object, i.e. iff $\mathrm{id}_{(\mathcal C_n)}=0$; as morphisms of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ are compared componentwise and the zero morphism is $(0)_n$, this holds iff $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_n}=0$, i.e. $\mathcal C_n=0$, for every $n\ge1$. Applied in the preadditive (abelian) category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ to $\alpha_1$ and its cokernel $q_1$, the same lemma gives: $\alpha_1$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules iff $\mathcal C_1=0$. So the statement is: $\mathcal C_n=0$ for all $n$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\mathcal C_1=0$. The direction $\Rightarrow$ is the case $n=1$; it remains to show that $\mathcal C_1=0$ implies $\mathcal C_n=0$ for every $n$ (steps 2-4).

source.place: Homology, Definition 010B and Lemma 010C (2) (surjective = Coker 0 = epimorphism); Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087X (coherent.tex line 6313): the cokernel in Coh(X, I) is the termwise cokernel

proof.text: (Affine pieces.) Assume $\mathcal C_1=0$ and fix $n\ge1$. As $X$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], it is covered by affine opens $U_j$ ($j\in J$) with $U_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ and $A_j=\mathcal O_X(U_j)$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Fix $j$, write $U=U_j$, $A=A_j$, $I=\mathcal I(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1), $U$ is a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I|_U$ a quasi-coherent ideal, and $\rho_U(\alpha)=(\alpha_n|_U):(\mathcal F_n|_U)\to(\mathcal G_n|_U)$ a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$; under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ the counit $\widetilde{I}\to\mathcal I|_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), so $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] to $A$, $I$ ($A^\wedge$ the $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]): $M=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U)$ and $N=\varprojlim_n\mathcal G_n(U)$ are finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules, the projections $p_n:M\to\mathcal F_n(U)$, $p_n:N\to\mathcal G_n(U)$ are surjective with kernels $I^nM$, $I^nN$ (part (1)), and $f=E(\rho_U\alpha)=\varprojlim_n\alpha_{n,U}:M\to N$ is $A^\wedge$-linear with $\alpha_{n,U}\circ p_n=p_n\circ f$ for all $n$ (part (2): $f$ is the limit of the compatible maps $\alpha_{n,U}=\Gamma(U,\alpha_n)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3), $\mathcal C_1(U)=\mathcal G_1(U)/\alpha_{1,U}(\mathcal F_1(U))$, so $\mathcal C_1=0$ gives that $\alpha_{1,U}$ is surjective. Hence $N=f(M)+IN$: for $y\in N$ choose $x\in M$ with $\alpha_{1,U}(p_1x)=p_1y$ ($p_1$ on $M$ is surjective); then $p_1(y-f(x))=p_1y-\alpha_{1,U}(p_1x)=0$, so $y-f(x)\in\ker p_1=IN$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Y (line 6396), hint of the omitted proof: 'Look on affine opens, use Lemma 087W and Algebra, Lemma 00DV'; Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine, line 6272), as used in the proof of Lemma 087X ('By Lemma 087W alpha corresponds to a map f : M -> N of finite A^-modules')

proof.text: (Nakayama over $A^\wedge$.) With the notation of step 2, let $Q=N/f(M)$, a finitely generated $A^\wedge$-module (a quotient of the finitely generated $N$), and $J=IA^\wedge\subseteq A^\wedge$. Since $I^1N=JN$ (notation of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine]), $N=f(M)+JN$ gives $JQ=Q$. As $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated, so $A^\wedge$ is $J$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (1); hence $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical]. By Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] (Stacks 00DV (2)), $Q=0$, i.e. $f:M\to N$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2), as the hint of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Y (coherent.tex line 6396) prescribes

proof.text: (Conclusion.) With $U=U_j$ as in steps 2-3: $\alpha_{n,U}\circ p_n=p_n\circ f$ is surjective ($f$ and $p_n:N\to\mathcal G_n(U)$ are), so $\alpha_{n,U}:\mathcal F_n(U)\to\mathcal G_n(U)$ is surjective and $\mathcal C_n(U)=\mathcal G_n(U)/\alpha_{n,U}(\mathcal F_n(U))=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3). The sheaf $\mathcal C_n$ is quasi-coherent (same node, (2)), hence so is $\mathcal C_n|_{U_j}$, and under $U_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ the counit $\widetilde{\mathcal C_n(U_j)}\to\mathcal C_n|_{U_j}$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3); so $\mathcal C_n|_{U_j}=0$ for every $j$. As the $U_j$ cover $X$, every section of $\mathcal C_n$ is locally zero, hence zero (sheaf axiom): $\mathcal C_n=0$. This holds for every $n$, so by step 1 $\alpha$ is an epimorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. Together with the direction $\Rightarrow$ of step 1 this proves the lemma.

split_report.summary: Split from the hint of Stacks 087Y (proof omitted there). Step 1 reduces both sides to cokernels: in Coh(X,I) the cokernel is termwise (087X node), and epi iff cokernel zero (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero, Stacks 010C(2), Mathlib Preadditive.epi_iff_isZero_cokernel'), so the claim is C_1 = 0 => C_n = 0. Steps 2-4: on a Noetherian affine cover, via 087W (lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine) alpha becomes f : M -> N of finite A^-modules with alpha_n = f mod I^n; C_1 = 0 gives N = f(M) + IN, and Nakayama (lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson, 00DV(2)) with IA^ in the Jacobson radical (lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (1), lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical) gives f surjective, hence C_n(U_j) = 0 and C_n = 0.
